source.author: verg
source.text: Postquam altos ventum in montis atque invia lustra, ecce ferae, saxi deiectae vertice, caprae decurrere iugis; alia de parte patentis transmittunt cursu campos atque agmina cervi pulverulenta fuga glomerant montisque relinquunt.
source.text_original: Postquam altos ventum in montis atque invia lustra, / ecce ferae, saxi deiectae vertice, caprae / decurrere iugis; alia de parte patentis / transmittunt cursu campos atque agmina cervi / pulverulenta fuga glomerant montisque relinquunt.
source.text_english: After they had come into the high mountains and pathless haunts, look, wild goats, driven down from the summit of a rock, came racing down the slopes; from another side deer, over the open plains, cross at a run and gather their dusty bands in flight and leave the mountains.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: at quibus arvorum studiumque insontis aratri, hos stimulant magnaque ratem per lustra viasque visi laude canunt manifesto in lumine Fauni silvarumque deae atque elatis cornibus Amnes.
reuse.text_original: at quibus arvorum studiumque insontis aratri, / hos stimulant magnaque ratem per lustra viasque / visi laude canunt manifesto in lumine Fauni / silvarumque deae atque elatis cornibus Amnes.
reuse.text_english: But those in whom there is a passion for the fields and for the guiltless plough, these are spurred on; and, as they are seen, they sing of the raft through the years and roads with great praise, in clear light, along with Fauni, the goddesses of the woods, and the Rivers with uplifted horns.
